chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Qasim ibn Bureyd, from Malik Al-Juhni, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Zakat of Fitra. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it to the Muslims. So if you do not find a Muslim, then give it to a weak one (poor Muslim), and give to your relative from it if you wish.'

key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Who should receive Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes a flexible hierarchy for Zakat al-Fitr, prioritizing the general Muslim community while allowing specific preference for the needy or one's own kin. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the primary intent is to purify the fasting person and support the community, with kinship ties serving as a valid, though not mandatory, channel for distribution. This flexibility underscores the practical application of zakat as both a spiritual purification and a social welfare mechanism.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Qasim Bin Bureyd, from Malik Al Juhny who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the Zakat of the Fitra. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should give it to the Muslims. So if you do not find a Muslim, so a weak one, and you can give to your relative from it if you so desire to’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Qasim ibn Yazid from Malik al- Juhaniy who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Zakat of al-Fitrah. He (the Imam) said, ‘Pay it to the Muslims. If you do not find one, pay to a Mustaz‘af (mentally and physically weak) or pay to your relatives, if you like.’”
